findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_service_status, check_service_status_url, recommend_monitoring, get_incident, review_coverage, review_noise, list_status_pages, get_status_page, search_service_catalog, change_member_access, get_my_notifications, list_webhooks, list_webhook_deliveries, update_webhook, test_webhook, plan_dependency, plan_content_check, update_monitor, draft_incident_post · Private data: recommend_monitoring, get_site, review_coverage, get_status_page, get_my_notifications, list_webhooks, add_webhook, update_webhook, test_webhook, plan_dependency, plan_dns_watch, update_status_page · Public sink: recommend_monitoring, get_incident, search_service_catalog, revoke_invitation, change_member_access, get_my_notifications, update_my_notifications, list_webhooks, list_webhook_deliveries, add_webhook, update_webhook, test_webhook, retry_webhook_delivery, plan_dependency, plan_status_page, draft_incident_post, publish_incident_post · Destructive: add_webhook, update_webhook, plan_site, plan_cron_monitor, update_monitor, set_anomaly_detection, dismiss_anomaly, remove_status_page_component.

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
